notes: Correct and tidy, with a defensive nil check and a doc update; it has a good table test of matcher-set classification and a POST integration test, but no direct `celmatcher` test and no end-to-end test of a `ph()`-based response retry.

Correct AST-based fix with a dynamic-name flag, a header-prefix length guard and a doc update; minor nit that `Placeholders()` returns the internal slice uncloned, but the table test is broad (`cel.bind`, near-miss names, escaped literals) and there is a POST integration test.

Well-encapsulated `ReferencesPlaceholder(predicate)` API with conservative dynamic handling and an updated field doc; an extensive table test covers `cel.bind`, nested `ph`, escaped literals and near-miss names, plus a POST body integration test.

Exposes a predicate-based `ReferencesPlaceholder` that cleanly encapsulates the dynamic/name check, correctly separates response placeholders, updates the docs, and tests a wide matrix including nested dynamic `ph()` and near-miss names.

Clean placeholder collection that dedupes names, resets on provision and returns a cloned slice, plus an accurate doc update; it has the most thorough tests: unit tests for `Placeholders`/`isResponsePlaceholder`/matcher-set classification and integration tests for request-only, escaped, near-miss and direct `ph()` cases.

Walks the checked AST for `ph()` calls with literal names, flags non-literal names as dynamic, and classifies response placeholders by exact name plus the header prefix; it also fixes the stale RetryMatchRaw doc and adds thorough unit and integration tests, including a direct `ph()` retry.

Correctly records the `ph()` names from the checked AST, flags dynamic names, and matches only the exact response placeholders; tests cover every mandated case end to end, but the stale `RetryMatchRaw` doc is left unchanged and `Placeholders()` exposes its internal slice.

Correct fix with strong behavioral tests (including 503 upstreams that must not be retried for non-response expressions); it leaves the RetryMatchRaw doc stale, and its last-argument heuristic and zero-arg early return are slightly loose.

Complete and well tested, with relevant docs. However, it drops zip members beneath a symlink even without --links, miscounting them as entries that escape the archive. It also refactors the squashfs List/NewObject path heavily (readDir/dirEntry, removing objectFromFileInfo).

Zip and squashfs both work with --links and add strong defence against hostile archives (members under symlinks, shadowed dirs, collisions, duplicates), with good tests and docs; however, the squashfs refactor adds an ancestor re-read (checkDir) on every List/NewObject even without --links, under-symlink drops are logged as 'escape the archive', and the link Open does not clamp negative offsets, so a suffix range larger than the target panics.

Implements --links for zip and squashfs, keeps List and NewObject consistent, and adds case-insensitive protection against members beneath a symlink only when --links is on. The cost is heavier machinery than the reference: a two-pass readZip, and checkParents re-reading every ancestor directory on each call.

Solid implementation for both backends: link filtering applies only with --links, matching is case-insensitive for destinations that fold case, and checkParents stops paths running through links; the shared zip/sqfs test with a copy-and-escape check is excellent, but the case-insensitive dropping can hide legitimate entries, readDir filters the slice in place, and a negative range offset can panic in the squashfs link Open.

Squashfs changes are close to the reference. On zip it keeps real entries and drops a conflicting symlink, which preserves data. It wrongly skips squashfs symlinks with an empty target and uses link != "" to mark a link, which the reference explicitly avoids.

A clean approach that defers zip links and drops any link conflicting with a directory, file or another link (which also handles nested links); the squashfs side is consistent between List and NewObject, Open clamps offsets properly, and tests are good; however, symlinks with empty targets are silently skipped, Info errors are swallowed, and squashfs dir/symlink name clashes are not guarded.

Works, but squashfs reads Links from each call's ctx rather than storing it at New (inconsistent with zip and changes signatures), and zip filters under-symlink members even without --links. The squashfs test builds its image with a process-global os.Chdir and creates symlinks without a Windows skip, which is fragile.

Correct zip handling (skips members inside symlinks, regular .rclonelink files win) and a workable squashfs lookup that relies on go-diskfs not following links; however, it reads --links from ctx at call time in squashfs but at construction in zip, changes function signatures, does not guard a squashfs dir/symlink name clash, has no negative-offset clamp, and its tests use a process-global os.Chdir hack.
